## Experimental Design 


There are many (too many) of teh detailed celltypes.

```{r}
table(sfe$celltype_SingleR2, sfe$tissue_sample)
```


## Check the niches

* The different shapes of these tissues means that no cell will really be random - cells are non-randomly arranged in the tissue themselves. Contrast that with a TMA where each sample exists within a round core. 

* Additionally there are very distinct tissue niches in this tissue. It may not make sense to consider the tissue as a whole. We will instead subset to a niche of 'the same type of strucutre' 


Plot all niches

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=15 eval=FALSE}
# make a named list of colours for the niches, using pals col25 palette.
# stops the colours swapping when a plot doesn't have all niches.
niche_cols <- pals::polychrome()[3:(length(levels(sfe$niche))+3)]
names(niche_cols) <- levels(sfe$niche)     
plot_one <- function(sample) {
  p <- plotSpatialFeature(sfe[,sfe$tissue_sample == sample], "niche",colGeometryName = "cellSeg") + 
    theme(legend.title=element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
    scale_fill_manual(values=niche_cols) +
    ggtitle(sample) 
  
  return(p)
}
samples <- levels(sfe$tissue_sample)
plots <- lapply(FUN=plot_one, X=samples)
p.all <- wrap_plots(plots, ncol=3)
plot(p.all)
```

## Build table for spicy

Why do some of these error out? Workin with crypt set which should have enough.

We are choosing to test cluster ids rather than the pretty celltypes - the inclusion of punctuation doesn't play nicely with some of the downstream functions.

```{r}
#cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe)), spatialCoords(sfe))
cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe.crypt)), spatialCoords(sfe.crypt))
#cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe.stromal)), spatialCoords(sfe.stromal))
#cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe.lymphoid)), spatialCoords(sfe.lymphoid))


# Filter to pair
cell_info         <- filter(cell_info, group %in% c('HC', 'CD'))
cell_info$group  <- droplevels(cell_info$group)
cell_info$tissue_sample  <- droplevels(cell_info$tissue_sample)

## Exclude celltypes that are very rare
# with fewr than this. (Very small number, to exclude 0)
min_cells <- 50
celltype_counts <- table(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info <- filter(cell_info, cluster_content %in% names(celltype_counts)[celltype_counts > min_cells])


# In cosmx, we have multiple 'images' for each sample. ANd that is explicytly handled ok.
# NB: From the docs: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/spicyR/inst/doc/spicyR.html
# **"spicyR supports mixed effects modelling when multiple images are obtained for each subject. In this case, subject is treated as a random effect and condition is treated as a fixed effect."**
#cell_info$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample),'_',cell_info$fov)
cell_info$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample))

cell_info$tissue_sample <-   as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample) # No UC 
  


# Workaround
# When there are a very small number  (specifically 1 or 2, 0 is fine)  of a given cell type within a given ImageID (FOV in our case), spicyR may yeild errors. 
# This may be more likely with very specific celltypes, or on cosmx data if we are using fovs as ImageID (e.g. edge of tissue.)
# This as of spicyR_1.22.0. Error ticket here; https://github.com/SydneyBioX/spicyR/issues/78 
# But, its not like 2 cells can be informative.
# So, as a workaround, removing cells that are are on a fov with less than 2 total of that given celltype. Ie. not removing the celltype, nor the fov, just 1-2 cells.
lonely_cells_table <- cell_info %>% group_by(imageID, cluster_code) %>%
  summarise(ncells=n()) %>% filter(ncells < 3 )  
lonely_cells_fovcluster <- paste0(lonely_cells_table$imageID, "-",lonely_cells_table$cluster_code)
cell_info <- cell_info[! (paste0(cell_info$imageID, "-",cell_info$cluster_code) %in% lonely_cells_fovcluster), ]



cell_info$cluster_content <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info$cluster_label   <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_label)
cell_info$cluster_code    <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_code)

# seem reasonable?
table(cell_info$cluster_code, cell_info$tissue_sample)



# rename x,y
cell_info <- cell_info %>% rename(
    x=CenterX_global_px, 
    y=CenterY_global_px,
)
# Check if this is still neccessary
# to avoid error: Error in owinInternalRect(xrange, yrange, ..., unitname = unitname): xrange should be a vector of length 2 giving (xmin, xmax)
min_x <- min(cell_info$x)
min_y <- min(cell_info$y)
if (min_x < 0) {cell_info$x = cell_info$x + -(min_x) + 1 }
if (min_y < 0) {cell_info$y = cell_info$y + -(min_y) + 1 }




```


TODO: Discuss Xenium / cosmx difference re ImageID and linear vs mixed model. Linear model should be pretty rare though.


## Run spicy
```{r}
spicy_res <- spicy(
          cells     = cell_info ,
          subject   = 'tissue_sample',
          cellType  = 'cluster_code',
          
          
          imageID   =  'imageID', # 'fov',
          #cellType  = 'cluster_content',
          #sigma     = 20, # explain this
          condition = 'group',
          
          # So its c7 and c12 that are problematic?
          #from='c2', to='c7' # seems so
          from='c7', to='c2'
          )
#  Your specified subject parameter has a one-to-one mapping with imageID. Converting to a linear model instead of mixed model.


#table(cell_info$cluster_code, cell_info$tissue_sample)
```


```{r}
topPairs(spicy_res )
```


Or, test all vs all

```{r}

spicy_res <- spicy(
          cells     = cell_info ,
          subject   = 'tissue_sample',
          #cellType  = 'cluster_code',
          cellType  = 'cluster_content',          # test with clusterc ontent.
          imageID   =  'imageID', 
          sigma     = 50, # explain this
          condition = 'group'
          )


```

```{r}
topPairs(spicy_res )
```

There is a very nice visualisation when you're testing two conditions, across all combinations

```{r}
signifPlot(spicy_res)
```

### Check out on tissue.

NB: with how small the fovs are, using fov as ImageID is giving pretty garbage results.


#### Crypt region - plasma and endothelia

```{r}
ggplot(filter(L_table_long, pair %in% c('c9__c11', "c11__c9", 'c14__c11', "c11__c14")), 
       aes(x=subject, y=L, col=condition)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.2) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~pair)

```




Why does c9__c11 plot as attraction (red) on the bubble plot?
         intercept coefficient      p.value  adj.pvalue from  to

c9__c11  -19.84347    45.83324 7.307680e-06 0.000822114   c9 c11

```{r}
interesting_celltypes <- c("c9: Endothelial Cells", "c11: Plasma Cells")

sfe.this$highlight <- ifelse (sfe.this$cluster_label %in% interesting_celltypes,
                         as.character(sfe.this$cluster_label),
                         sfe.this$highlight)

# Add the L statistic in as cell metadata, so we can plot it spatially.

L_table_pair_lookup <- set_names(L_table_long_pair$L, nm=L_table_long_pair$imageID)

  'c11: Plasma Cells' = "purple4" ,  
  #'c14: Plasma Cells' = "royalblue" ,
  'Other'      = "grey80"
)
```

```{r}
interesting_celltypes <- c("Monocytic Cells", "Intestinal Epithelial Cells")

crypt_niches <- c("n2",'n3','n4', 'n7')

sfe.this <- sfe[,sfe$niche %in% crypt_niches]

sfe.this$highlight <- "Other"

                         as.character(sfe.this$cluster_content),
                         sfe.this$highlight)

# Add the L statistic in as cell metadata, so we can plot it spatially.
L_table_long_pair <- filter(L_table_long, pair == "Monocytic Cells__Monocytic Cells")
L_table_pair_lookup <- set_names(L_table_long_pair$L, nm=L_table_long_pair$imageID)

sfe.this$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(sfe.this$tissue_sample),'_',sfe.this$fov)
sfe.this$L_monomono <- L_table_pair_lookup[as.character(sfe.this$imageID)]



highlight_cols <- c(
  'Monocytic Cells'= 'red',
  'Intestinal Epithelial Cells' = "blue" ,  
  #'c14: Plasma Cells' = "royalblue" ,
  'Other'      = "grey80"
)
```

### Aside: get L statistics for all samples

In more complex experiments you might want to pull out the L values to run
own statistical tests, or simply plot L values of all groups together. Here 
by not filtering to out the UC samples, we can plot the HC, UC and CD samples all together.

```{r}
cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe.stromal)), spatialCoords(sfe.stromal))

## Exclude celltypes that are very rare
# with fewr than this. (Very small number, to exclude 0)
min_cells <- 50
celltype_counts <- table(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info <- filter(cell_info, cluster_content %in% names(celltype_counts)[celltype_counts > min_cells])


# In cosmx, we have multiple 'images' for each sample. ANd that is explicytly handled ok.
# NB: From the docs: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/spicyR/inst/doc/spicyR.html
# **"spicyR supports mixed effects modelling when multiple images are obtained for each subject. In this case, subject is treated as a random effect and condition is treated as a fixed effect."**
cell_info$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample),'_',cell_info$fov)
cell_info$tissue_sample <-   as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample) # No UC 
  
# Workaround
# When there are a very small number  (specifically 1 or 2, 0 is fine)  of a given cell type within a given ImageID (FOV in our case), spicyR may yeild errors. 
# This may be more likely with very specific celltypes, or on cosmx data if we are using fovs as ImageID (e.g. edge of tissue.)
# This as of spicyR_1.22.0. Error ticket here; https://github.com/SydneyBioX/spicyR/issues/78 
# But, its not like 2 cells can be informative.
# So, as a workaround, removing cells that are are on a fov with less than 2 total of that given celltype. Ie. not removing the celltype, nor the fov, just 1-2 cells.
lonely_cells_table <- cell_info %>% group_by(imageID, cluster_code) %>%
  summarise(ncells=n()) %>% filter(ncells < 3 )  
lonely_cells_fovcluster <- paste0(lonely_cells_table$imageID, "-",lonely_cells_table$cluster_code)
cell_info <- cell_info[! (paste0(cell_info$imageID, "-",cell_info$cluster_code) %in% lonely_cells_fovcluster), ]


cell_info$cluster_content <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info$cluster_label   <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_label)
cell_info$cluster_code    <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_code)

# seem reasonable?
table(cell_info$cluster_code, cell_info$tissue_sample)



# rename x,y
cell_info <- cell_info %>% rename(
    x=CenterX_global_px, 
    y=CenterY_global_px,
)
# Check if this is still neccessary
# to avoid error: Error in owinInternalRect(xrange, yrange, ..., unitname = unitname): xrange should be a vector of length 2 giving (xmin, xmax)
min_x <- min(cell_info$x)
min_y <- min(cell_info$y)
if (min_x < 0) {cell_info$x = cell_info$x + -(min_x) + 1 }
if (min_y < 0) {cell_info$y = cell_info$y + -(min_y) + 1 }


spicy_res <- spicy(
          cells     = cell_info ,
          subject   = 'tissue_sample',
          cellType  = 'cluster_code',
          imageID   =  'imageID', 
          sigma     = 20, # explain this
          condition = 'group'
          )


# L_function_table <- get_L_function_table(spicy_res)
L_table <- bind(spicy_res)
L_table_long <- pivot_longer(L_table, cols=! c(imageID, condition, subject ),
                             names_to = 'pair', values_to="L") %>%
  filter(! is.na(L)) # Remove pairs not tested, where L is NA


```

```{r}
ggplot(filter(L_table_long, pair %in% c('c3__c3', 'c4__c4', 'c5__c5', 'c4__c5', 'c4__c4')), 
       aes(x=subject, y=L, col=condition)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.2) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~pair)
```

```{r}
       aes(x=subject, y=L, col=condition)) +

  theme_bw() 
```

## ASIDE: What level of Image ID?

(Move this somewhere else. )

Given the following experiment

Slide 1 : sample 1 : covered by 10 fovs
Slide 2 : sample 2 : covered by 10 fovs


1. One entry per celltype per FOV per tissue sample? ImageID = Sample.   (1:1 ImageID:Sample)
2. One entry per celltype per FOV per tissue sample? And ImageID = fov.  (m:1 ImageID:Sample)


Dsicussion on L function; https://github.com/SydneyBioX/spicyR/issues/58
*"That's right! You'd get one L-function value for each cell type pair/image combination. Having multiple images per subject only affects the final linear model that's built. Hope this clears things up!"*

Hmm..

From reading (https://us.sagepub.com/sites/default/files/upm-binaries/47528_ch_1.pdf) seems like a mixed model can cope perfectly fine with multiple images per fov (apparently good for repeated observations, or observations at multiple levels ), and should be able to test 'sample' without treating the mtuliple images as a billion replicates. And can handle the 'interaction terms' of variance across overlapping factors (e.g. ind + condition) implicetly. E.g. if we had multipel samples per slide that would model the slide variance, and the sample variance in its m:m glory (and the heircially lower fov variance too?).


the answer is 2: from the docs: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/spicyR/inst/doc/spicyR.html

**"spicyR supports mixed effects modelling when multiple images are obtained for each subject. In this case, subject is treated as a random effect and condition is treated as a fixed effect."**



```{r}
cell_info.1 <- cell_info
cell_info.2 <- cell_info
cell_info.2$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(paste0(cell_info.2$sample_id,'_',cell_info.2$fov) ))
                                 
table(cell_info.1$sample_id, cell_info.1$imageID)                                 
table(cell_info.2$sample_id, cell_info.2$imageID)                                 
```


```{r}
spicy_res.1 <- spicy(
          cells     = cell_info ,
          subject   = 'tissue_sample',
          cellType  = 'highlight',
          condition = 'group'
          )
#  Your specified subject parameter has a one-to-one mapping with imageID. Converting to a linear model instead of mixed model.

spicy_res.2 <- spicy(
          cells     = cell_info.2 ,
          subject   = 'tissue_sample',
          cellType  = 'highlight',
          #sigma     = 20, # explain this
          condition = 'group'
          )
```

```{r}
cell_info <- cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sfe)), spatialCoords(sfe))

# Filter to pair
cell_info         <- filter(cell_info, group %in% c('HC', 'CD'))
cell_info$group  <- droplevels(cell_info$group)
cell_info$tissue_sample  <- droplevels(cell_info$tissue_sample)

## Exclude celltypes that are very rare
# with fewr than this. (Very small number, to exclude 0)
min_cells <- 50
celltype_counts <- table(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info <- filter(cell_info, cluster_content %in% names(celltype_counts)[celltype_counts > min_cells])


# In cosmx, we have multiple 'images' for each sample. ANd that is explicytly handled ok.
# NB: From the docs: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/spicyR/inst/doc/spicyR.html
# **"spicyR supports mixed effects modelling when multiple images are obtained for each subject. In this case, subject is treated as a random effect and condition is treated as a fixed effect."**
#cell_info$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample),'_',cell_info$fov)
cell_info$imageID    <- paste0(as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample))

cell_info$tissue_sample <-   as.character(cell_info$tissue_sample) # No UC 
  


# Workaround
# When there are a very small number  (specifically 1 or 2, 0 is fine)  of a given cell type within a given ImageID (FOV in our case), spicyR may yeild errors. 
# This may be more likely with very specific celltypes, or on cosmx data if we are using fovs as ImageID (e.g. edge of tissue.)
# This as of spicyR_1.22.0. Error ticket here; https://github.com/SydneyBioX/spicyR/issues/78 
# But, its not like 2 cells can be informative.
# So, as a workaround, removing cells that are are on a fov with less than 2 total of that given celltype. Ie. not removing the celltype, nor the fov, just 1-2 cells.
lonely_cells_table <- cell_info %>% group_by(imageID, cluster_code) %>%
  summarise(ncells=n()) %>% filter(ncells < 3 )  
lonely_cells_fovcluster <- paste0(lonely_cells_table$imageID, "-",lonely_cells_table$cluster_code)
cell_info <- cell_info[! (paste0(cell_info$imageID, "-",cell_info$cluster_code) %in% lonely_cells_fovcluster), ]



cell_info$cluster_content <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_content)
cell_info$cluster_label   <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_label)
cell_info$cluster_code    <- droplevels(cell_info$cluster_code)

cell_info$toplevel    <- as.factor(cell_info$toplevel)


# seem reasonable?
table(cell_info$cluster_code, cell_info$tissue_sample)

# Convert px to um
# um per pixel can vary between experimenrts.
#https://github.com/jinworks/CellChat/issues/292
# https://nanostring-biostats.github.io/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/posts/flat-file-exports/flat-files-compare.html
#Thus, to convert to microns multiply the pixel value by 0.12028 m per pixel.
um_per_pixel <- 0.12028 
cell_info$x <-cell_info$CenterX_global_px * um_per_pixel
cell_info$y <-cell_info$CenterY_global_px * um_per_pixel

# Check if this is still neccessary
# to avoid error: Error in owinInternalRect(xrange, yrange, ..., unitname = unitname): xrange should be a vector of length 2 giving (xmin, xmax)
min_x <- min(cell_info$x)
min_y <- min(cell_info$y)
if (min_x < 0) {cell_info$x = cell_info$x + -(min_x) + 1 }
if (min_y < 0) {cell_info$y = cell_info$y + -(min_y) + 1 }


```


What radius is important for context. I think we are using different units (x and y are pixes!)
```{r}
# quick and dirty plot to see the radius
radius <- seq(50, 550, 50)
cell_info.this <- filter(cell_info, imageID == "HC_c")
xpos <- mean(c(min(cell_info.this$x), max(cell_info.this$x)))
ypos <- mean(c(min(cell_info.this$y), max(cell_info.this$y)))
circle_scales <- bind_cols(radius=radius, x=xpos, y=ypos)

ggplot(cell_info.this, aes(x=x, y=y, col=toplevel)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_circle(data=circle_scales, mapping=aes(x0=x,y0=y, r=radius ), col='black')   +
  theme_bw()

```


```{r}


# Get all relationships between cell types and their parents
parentDf <- parentCombinations(
  all = levels(cell_info$cluster_code),
  parentList = biologicalHierarchy
)


# Running Kontextual on all relationships across all images.
resKontextual.full <- Kontextual(
  cells         = cell_info,
  parentDf      = parentDf,
  spatialCoords = c("x","y"),
  cellType      = 'cluster_code',
  r = 100,
  cores = 8,
```

```{r}
weightFunction <- spicyR:::getWeightFunction(pairwiseAssoc, nCells, m1, m2, BPPARAM, weights, weightsByPair, weightFactor)



#' @importFrom BiocParallel bpmapply
getWeightFunction <- function(
    pairwiseAssoc,
    nCells,
    m1,
    m2,
    BPPARAM,
    weights,
    weightsByPair,
    weightFactor) {
  if (!weights) {
    weightFunction <- rep(1, nrow(pairwiseAssoc) * ncol(pairwiseAssoc))
    pair <- rep(colnames(pairwiseAssoc), each = nrow(pairwiseAssoc))
    weightFunction <- split(weightFunction, pair)
    return(weightFunction)
  }


  resSq <- apply(pairwiseAssoc, 2, function(x) {
    if (sum(!is.na(x)) > 1) {
      if (stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
        return((x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))^2)
      } else {
        return(rep(NA, length(x)))
      }
    } else {
      return(rep(NA, length(x)))
    }
  })

  if (weightsByPair) {
    weightFunction <- BiocParallel::bpmapply(
      calcWeights,
      rS = as.list(as.data.frame(resSq)), M1 = m1, M2 = m2, BPPARAM = BPPARAM,
      MoreArgs = list(nCells = nCells, weightFactor), SIMPLIFY = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    weightFunction <- calcWeights(m1, m2, rS = resSq, nCells, weightFactor)
    pair <- rep(colnames(pairwiseAssoc), each = nrow(pairwiseAssoc))
    weightFunction <- split(weightFunction, pair)
  }
  weightFunction[colnames(pairwiseAssoc)]
}

#' @importFrom scam scam
#' @importFrom stats quantile
calcWeights <- function(rS, M1, M2, nCells, weightFactor) {
  count1 <- as.vector(nCells[, M1])
  count2 <- as.vector(nCells[, M2])
  rS <- as.vector(rS)
  toWeight <- !is.na(rS)
  resSqToWeight <- rS[toWeight]
  count1ToWeight <- count1[toWeight]
  count2ToWeight <- count2[toWeight]
  if (length(count1ToWeight) <= 20) {
    warning("A cell type pair is seen less than 20 times, not using weights for this pair.") # nolint
    weightFunction <- rep(1, length(count1))
    return(weightFunction)
  }
  weightFunction <- scam::scam(
    log10(resSqToWeight + 1) ~ s(log10(count1ToWeight + 1), bs = "mpd") + s(log10(count2ToWeight + 1), bs = "mpd") # nolint
  ) # , optimizer = "nlm.fd")

  z1 <- suppressWarnings(stats::predict(weightFunction, data.frame(
    count1ToWeight = as.numeric(count1),
    count2ToWeight = as.numeric(count2)
  )))
  w <- 1 / pmax(z1, stats::quantile(z1[z1 > 0.1], 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))
  w <- w / mean(w, na.rm = TRUE)
  w^weightFactor
}

```
